title: Immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) in adults
subject: haematology-oncology
summary: ITP is a diagnosis of exclusion. Treat newly diagnosed adults with platelets below 30 x 10^9/L or bleeding using prednisolone 0.5 to 2 mg/kg/day (6 weeks or less in total) or dexamethasone 40 mg daily for 4 days, add IVIg 1 g/kg for bleeding or when a rapid rise is needed, and escalate urgently for life-threatening bleeding.

sections.title: Recognise
items: Isolated thrombocytopenia (platelets below 100 x 10^9/L) with an otherwise normal blood count and film. Bleeding is usually mucocutaneous: petechiae, purpura, epistaxis, gum bleeding, menorrhagia. Many patients are asymptomatic.

Exclude pseudothrombocytopenia (EDTA clumping: check the film or a citrate sample), drugs, alcohol and liver disease, HIV, hepatitis C, H. pylori, SLE and antiphospholipid syndrome, lymphoproliferative disease, TTP, HIT, DIC and marrow failure.
In India, fever with thrombocytopenia is usually dengue, malaria, scrub typhus or sepsis, not ITP.
Phases: newly diagnosed (up to 3 months), persistent (3 to 12 months), chronic (more than 12 months). Bleeding risk is higher with older age, prior bleeding and anticoagulant or antiplatelet use.

sections.title: Investigations
items: FBC with blood film reviewed by a haematologist, reticulocytes, renal and liver function.
HIV and hepatitis C testing in all adults; hepatitis B before rituximab; H. pylori testing; pregnancy test where relevant; ANA and antiphospholipid antibodies if clinical features.
Dengue NS1 or serology and a malaria test if febrile.
Bone marrow examination is not needed for typical ITP at any age; do it for atypical features (other cytopenias, abnormal film, lymphadenopathy or organomegaly) or failure of first-line therapy.

sections.title: When to treat and first-line (ASH 2019)
items: Platelets 30 x 10^9/L or more, asymptomatic or minor mucocutaneous bleeding: observe without steroids (strong recommendation), unless comorbidity, anticoagulant or antiplatelet use, upcoming procedure, or age above 60 years.
Newly diagnosed, platelets below 30 x 10^9/L, asymptomatic or minor bleeding: corticosteroids rather than observation.

Prednisolone 0.5 to 2 mg/kg/day orally (commonly 1 mg/kg, maximum 80 mg), with total duration including taper of 6 weeks or less. Or dexamethasone 40 mg daily for 4 days, preferred when a faster response matters.
IVIg 1 g/kg IV once, repeated once if needed, with steroids when a rapid rise is required (bleeding, urgent procedure) or when steroids are contraindicated.

Newly diagnosed with platelets below 20 x 10^9/L: admission is suggested. Established ITP with platelets below 20 and minor bleeding: outpatient care with urgent haematology review. Arrange haematology follow-up within 24 to 72 hours of diagnosis or relapse.
Monitor steroid effects: BP, glucose, mood and sleep, gastric symptoms, glaucoma, myopathy and bone health.

sections.title: Emergency: life-threatening or critical-site bleeding
items: Intracranial, major GI or other life-threatening bleeding, or emergency surgery: resuscitate and involve haematology immediately.
Give together: IVIg 1 g/kg IV (repeat the next day if needed), methylprednisolone 1 g IV daily for 3 days, and platelet transfusion (repeated or larger doses despite short survival).
Add tranexamic acid 1 g IV every 8 hours for mucosal bleeding. Stop antiplatelet and anticoagulant drugs.
If bleeding continues: thrombopoietin receptor agonist and, rarely, emergency splenectomy on haematology advice.

sections.title: Second-line (steroid-dependent or unresponsive)
items: Options: thrombopoietin receptor agonist (eltrombopag, romiplostim), rituximab, or splenectomy; ASH suggests a TPO-RA or splenectomy, rituximab over splenectomy, and a TPO-RA over rituximab. Choose with the patient.

Eltrombopag 50 mg orally once daily (25 mg in East or Southeast Asian ancestry or hepatic impairment), on an empty stomach away from dairy, antacids and calcium; titrate to platelets 50 x 10^9/L or more, maximum 75 mg daily.
Romiplostim 1 mcg/kg SC weekly, adjusted by 1 mcg/kg weekly to platelets 50 x 10^9/L or more, maximum 10 mcg/kg.
Rituximab 375 mg/m2 IV weekly for 4 doses after hepatitis B screening.
Delay splenectomy at least 12 months from diagnosis because spontaneous remission is possible; vaccinate against encapsulated bacteria beforehand.

sections.title: Special situations
items: Pregnancy: corticosteroids or IVIg if treatment is needed; mode of delivery on obstetric grounds; plan neuraxial anaesthesia with the anaesthetist.
Procedures: raise the count with IVIg or steroids beforehand rather than relying on platelet transfusion.
Positive H. pylori: eradicate. HIV or hepatitis C: treat the infection with specialist input.
Patients needing anticoagulant or antiplatelet therapy: plan with haematology.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Treating a count of 30 x 10^9/L or more without bleeding or risk factors.
Prolonged steroid courses beyond 6 weeks.
Routine platelet transfusion outside life-threatening bleeding (short survival and little benefit).
Missing pseudothrombocytopenia, TTP, HIT, drug-induced thrombocytopenia, dengue or HIV.

drugs.name: Prednisolone
drugs.dose: 0.5 to 2 mg/kg/day orally (commonly 1 mg/kg, maximum 80 mg), tapered so the total course is 6 weeks or less
drugs.notes: First line for platelets below 30 x 10^9/L or bleeding.

drugs.name: Dexamethasone
drugs.dose: 40 mg orally or IV once daily for 4 days
drugs.notes: Faster response at 7 days than prednisolone.

drugs.name: IV immunoglobulin (IVIg)
drugs.dose: 1 g/kg IV once, repeat once if needed
drugs.notes: Bleeding, rapid rise needed, or steroids contraindicated. Watch renal function, thrombosis and headache.

drugs.name: Methylprednisolone
drugs.dose: 1 g IV once daily for 3 days
drugs.notes: Life-threatening bleeding, with IVIg and platelets.

drugs.name: Tranexamic acid
drugs.notes: Adjunct for mucosal bleeding. Reduce in renal impairment.

drugs.name: Eltrombopag
drugs.dose: 50 mg orally once daily (25 mg in East or Southeast Asian ancestry or hepatic impairment), maximum 75 mg

drugs.name: Romiplostim
drugs.dose: 1 mcg/kg SC weekly, titrate by 1 mcg/kg weekly, maximum 10 mcg/kg
